title: Verification Method Matcher
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Matching activity in which learners recommend one of five verification methods (known-answer test, independent method, primary source check, cross-model check, replication) for each of eight illustrative AI-assisted claims. Eight claims in a fixed order, one attempt each; the correct method is always revealed with a one-sentence reason, and the run ends with a score out of 8, a mastery statement at 7 of 8, and the claims grouped by method.

educational.topic: Choosing a verification method for AI-assisted research claims
learningObjectives: Recommend which of five verification methods best fits each of eight AI-assisted claims, with at least 7 of 8 matching the answer key
prerequisites: Known-answer test, independent method, primary source check, cross-model check, and replication, as defined in the section Kinds of Checks of Chapter 17

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; the method list is a native select and all actions are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and the symbols check mark and X as well as a color-blind-safe blue and orange pair; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Choose a method
controls.purpose: Chooses one of the five verification methods for the current claim. Starts with no method chosen and is disabled after the answer is submitted.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Commits the chosen method for the current claim. Enabled only when a method is chosen; one attempt per claim.

controls.label: Next Claim / See Score / Start Over
controls.purpose: Enabled after an answer is submitted. Advances to the next claim, shows the score after claim 8, and on the summary screen starts a new run of the same eight claims.

controls.label: Next Page
controls.purpose: Shown only on the summary screen when the claims grouped by method do not fit on one page; pages through the groups.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Forced choice among five methods with one attempt per item, immediate explanatory feedback, and a summary that groups the items by method
keyQuestions: What could be wrong with this claim, and which check would reveal it?
Is the claim about an implementation, a method, a quotation, a screening question, or recurrence?
Does the check have different failure causes from the thing being checked?
commonMisconceptions: Asking the same model again is an independent check
A cross-model check proves a claim
A single check method suits every claim
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score of at least 7 of 8 methods matching the answer key is evidence of mastery
Reading the table of methods is exploration and is not evidence
Learner explains each missed claim using the Why sentence and what the claim could be wrong about
